title: Course 1 Integrated Cultivation Workflow Practical

criteria.title: Recognize seeded hazards and immediate controls
criteria.fullCredit: Identifies all seeded blocking hazards and applies the supplied immediate controls without normalizing or bypassing them.
criteria.partialCredit: Identifies the major hazard pattern but misses one lower-severity control, needs a permitted prompt, or records an incomplete control rationale.
criteria.noCredit: Misses a blocking hazard, treats an explicit unsafe condition as acceptable, or proposes continuing without the required control.

criteria.title: Use supplied PPE and chemical safety information
criteria.fullCredit: Uses the supplied task, label, SDS, and employer PPE information correctly and does not invent protection requirements or chemical directions.
criteria.partialCredit: Locates the correct information but needs a permitted prompt to connect one requirement to the task or omits a non-blocking detail.
criteria.noCredit: Selects PPE or chemical handling from guesswork, ignores supplied requirements, or proceeds when required information is missing.

criteria.title: Stay inside authority and use stop-work/escalation
criteria.fullCredit: Correctly distinguishes routine technician controls from protected work and stops or escalates the seeded condition without attempting unauthorized repair.
criteria.partialCredit: Recognizes the authority boundary after a permitted prompt or escalates correctly but gives an incomplete explanation of why work cannot continue.
criteria.noCredit: Attempts protected servicing, bypasses an explicit stop condition, or continues work after the supplied procedure requires escalation.

criteria.title: Create a useful safety decision record
criteria.fullCredit: Records the hazard, immediate control, affected task or area, notification, and open next action accurately enough for another worker to reconstruct the decision.
criteria.partialCredit: Records the main condition and response but omits one useful context element such as time, affected identity, notification, or open action.
criteria.noCredit: Creates a misleading or unusable record, omits the unsafe condition, or documents completion when the safety decision remains open.

criteria.title: Recognize contamination and movement pathways
criteria.fullCredit: Identifies the seeded people, tool, material, or room movement pathway that could spread contamination and chooses the supplied control sequence.
criteria.partialCredit: Recognizes the main pathway but misses one secondary transfer point or needs a permitted prompt to complete the movement-control reasoning.
criteria.noCredit: Fails to identify the relevant pathway or proposes movement that defeats the supplied contamination-control boundary.

criteria.title: Execute the supplied cleaning and sanitation sequence
criteria.fullCredit: Follows the supplied cleaning/sanitation sequence in order, distinguishes debris removal from sanitation, and verifies the defined completion condition.
criteria.partialCredit: Completes the core sequence but needs one permitted prompt, omits one noncritical verification step, or gives an incomplete explanation of sequence purpose.
criteria.noCredit: Skips a required blocking step, reverses the sequence in a way that defeats the process, or invents an unsupported chemical procedure.

criteria.title: Respect quarantine, hold, REI, and movement restrictions
criteria.fullCredit: Correctly distinguishes the supplied plant-health hold/quarantine status from pesticide restricted-entry status and respects every active movement or access restriction.
criteria.partialCredit: Respects the restriction but needs a permitted prompt to name the controlling status or to explain which separate restriction remains active.
criteria.noCredit: Bypasses an explicit hold or restricted-entry control, treats different statuses as interchangeable, or moves material through a prohibited boundary.

criteria.title: Stay inside product and procedure authorization
criteria.fullCredit: Uses only the supplied authorized product and procedure information and escalates when a substitution or instruction is not explicitly supported.
criteria.partialCredit: Recognizes that authorization is required but needs a permitted prompt to stop before selecting an unsupported substitute.
criteria.noCredit: Invents chemical directions, substitutes a product without supplied authorization, or treats a general practice as a facility-specific instruction.

criteria.title: Verify the current controlled instruction
criteria.fullCredit: Confirms the correct task, document identity, revision, scope, prerequisites, and applicable work order before acting.
criteria.partialCredit: Finds the correct instruction but needs a permitted prompt to verify one control element such as revision, scope, or prerequisite.
criteria.noCredit: Uses an obsolete, wrong-scope, or otherwise uncontrolled instruction when the current controlled source is available.

criteria.title: Execute required steps and acceptance criteria
criteria.fullCredit: Performs the supplied required steps in the controlled sequence and verifies the defined acceptance criteria before declaring the task complete.
criteria.partialCredit: Completes the main steps but misses one noncritical acceptance detail or requires a permitted prompt to verify completion evidence.
criteria.noCredit: Skips a required blocking step, changes the procedure without authority, or declares completion without required acceptance evidence.

criteria.title: Handle missing or conflicting instructions
criteria.fullCredit: Recognizes missing, conflicting, or unclear instructions and stops or escalates rather than selecting an unsupported workaround.
criteria.partialCredit: Recognizes the conflict after a permitted prompt or escalates correctly but does not fully identify the unresolved instruction question.
criteria.noCredit: Chooses an unauthorized workaround, invents a requirement, or continues despite a controlling instruction conflict.

criteria.title: Document deviations and incomplete work honestly
criteria.fullCredit: Records what was completed, what remains open, the deviation or exception status, and the next authorized action without manufacturing completion.
criteria.partialCredit: Preserves the open status but omits one context element or needs a permitted prompt to distinguish a planned exception from an unplanned deviation.
criteria.noCredit: Marks incomplete work complete, hides a deviation, or backfills missing status information as though it were contemporaneous.

criteria.title: Verify physical identity before movement
criteria.fullCredit: Verifies the controlled physical identity against the supplied record before movement and detects the seeded mismatch before identity can be lost.
criteria.partialCredit: Performs the identity check but needs a permitted prompt to resolve one label/record comparison or to identify a secondary mismatch cue.
criteria.noCredit: Moves material without the required identity check, ignores an obvious mismatch, or relies on appearance instead of controlled identity.

criteria.title: Preserve source, destination, time, and event context
criteria.fullCredit: Records the source, destination, material identity, quantity or status as applicable, time, and responsible event context needed to reconstruct the movement.
criteria.partialCredit: Captures the core movement but omits one reconstructability element or needs a permitted prompt to connect the event to the correct controlled record.
criteria.noCredit: Creates an ambiguous movement record that cannot identify what moved, from where, to where, or under which controlled identity.

criteria.title: Block and preserve identity discrepancies
criteria.fullCredit: Stops the discrepant movement, preserves both physical and record evidence, and escalates without relabeling or forcing a match.
criteria.partialCredit: Stops the movement but needs a permitted prompt to preserve one piece of evidence or to identify the proper escalation owner.
criteria.noCredit: Forces the physical material to match the record, relabels without authorization, or continues movement through an unresolved discrepancy.

criteria.title: Maintain genealogy through handoff
criteria.fullCredit: Preserves enough linked identity/event information that another worker can reconstruct the material genealogy and current unresolved status at handoff.
criteria.partialCredit: Preserves the main identity chain but omits one noncritical link or needs a permitted prompt to connect an open event to the handoff.
criteria.noCredit: Breaks the identity chain, loses the relationship between source and resulting material, or hands off an unresolved identity issue without controlled identifiers.

criteria.title: Compare physical evidence with the controlled record
criteria.fullCredit: Performs the supplied physical-versus-record comparison using the correct identifiers and quantities without forcing either side to match the other.
criteria.partialCredit: Completes the comparison but needs a permitted prompt to verify one identifier, unit, or source record before interpreting the difference.
criteria.noCredit: Skips the comparison, substitutes an estimate for physical evidence, or changes a record solely to eliminate the discrepancy.

criteria.title: Separate confirmed facts from unresolved facts
criteria.fullCredit: Clearly distinguishes observed counts/identities/events from hypotheses, missing information, and decisions that remain unresolved.
criteria.partialCredit: Mostly separates fact from hypothesis but uses one ambiguous statement or needs a permitted prompt to identify what is still unknown.
criteria.noCredit: Presents a guess as a confirmed fact or invents a cause, count, identity, or disposition to make the records reconcile.

criteria.title: Preserve discrepancy evidence
criteria.fullCredit: Preserves the relevant record, physical status, identifiers, timing, and observations needed for an authorized follow-up decision.
criteria.partialCredit: Preserves the main evidence but omits one context element that can still be recovered from the controlled packet.
criteria.noCredit: Destroys, overwrites, or obscures evidence needed to reconstruct the discrepancy.

criteria.title: Escalate disposition decisions to the authorized process
criteria.fullCredit: Routes the discrepancy to the correct supplied role/process and does not independently release, destroy, relabel, or adjust material outside Technician I authority.
criteria.partialCredit: Recognizes that escalation is required but needs a permitted prompt to identify the correct decision owner or required supporting information.
criteria.noCredit: Makes an unauthorized disposition or inventory adjustment, or treats reconciliation as permission to erase the unresolved event.

criteria.title: Complete permitted pre-use readiness checks
criteria.fullCredit: Completes the supplied external readiness checks, verifies the defined ready/not-ready conditions, and records the relevant observations before use.
criteria.partialCredit: Completes the major checks but misses one noncritical supplied check or needs a permitted prompt to verify a readiness condition.
criteria.noCredit: Uses the equipment without required readiness checks or ignores an explicit not-ready condition.

criteria.title: Stay inside the operator-care boundary
criteria.fullCredit: Performs only explicitly assigned operator-level cleaning, inspection, or routine care and stops before protected servicing, repair, or energized technical work.
criteria.partialCredit: Recognizes the boundary after a permitted prompt or correctly stops but gives an incomplete explanation of which task requires qualified service.
criteria.noCredit: Attempts protected servicing, removes guards, defeats safety controls, or undertakes repair outside the supplied Technician I authority.

criteria.title: Describe faults without unsupported diagnosis
criteria.fullCredit: Records observable symptoms, timing, alarms, conditions, and recurrence without presenting an unsupported root-cause diagnosis as fact.
criteria.partialCredit: Records the main symptom but omits one useful observation or uses tentative diagnostic language that is clearly labeled as unconfirmed.
criteria.noCredit: Invents a confirmed cause, changes the record to fit a guess, or omits the observable fault condition.

criteria.title: Escalate recurring or unsafe faults appropriately
criteria.fullCredit: Stops or limits use as required, preserves the recurring-fault timeline, and routes the equipment to the supplied authorized maintenance/escalation process.
criteria.partialCredit: Escalates correctly but needs a permitted prompt to preserve the recurrence history or identify the exact affected asset/status.
criteria.noCredit: Repeatedly resets or works around the fault, continues unsafe operation, or fails to communicate the unresolved equipment status.

criteria.title: Create timely, context-rich records
criteria.fullCredit: Records observations/actions with the identity, unit, location, time, and other task context needed for another qualified person to reconstruct the event.
criteria.partialCredit: Records the core fact but omits one useful context element or needs a permitted prompt to distinguish observation time from later entry time.
criteria.noCredit: Backdates, creates a context-free value that cannot be interpreted, or represents remembered information as a contemporaneous record.

criteria.title: Preserve attribution and readable meaning
criteria.fullCredit: Ensures the record/change is attributable to the responsible person or controlled system and is readable and unambiguous for the intended workflow.
criteria.partialCredit: Record meaning is clear but attribution or one contextual label needs a permitted correction before the packet can be considered complete.
criteria.noCredit: Creates an anonymous, ambiguous, or otherwise non-reconstructable entry when controlled attribution is required.

criteria.title: Correct records while preserving original history
criteria.fullCredit: Uses the supplied correction method so the original entry remains understandable and the correction, author, timing, and required reason can be reconstructed.
criteria.partialCredit: Recognizes the need for a controlled correction but needs a permitted prompt to preserve one history element or complete the correction context.
criteria.noCredit: Silently overwrites, erases, destroys, or replaces the original record history.

criteria.title: Handle missing and late data honestly
criteria.fullCredit: Keeps missing data visibly missing and uses the supplied late-entry or exception process without substituting targets, averages, or remembered estimates as original facts.
criteria.partialCredit: Recognizes the missing/late-data issue but needs a permitted prompt to document the true timing or to separate an estimate from controlled data.
criteria.noCredit: Fabricates a missing value, assigns it the original time, or hides the fact that required data were not captured.

criteria.title: Communicate completed work accurately
criteria.fullCredit: States what was completed and the current verified status without overstating incomplete work or requiring the receiver to infer what happened.
criteria.partialCredit: Communicates the main completed work but omits one useful status detail or needs a permitted prompt to distinguish completion from pending verification.
criteria.noCredit: Misrepresents incomplete work as complete or omits a completed action that materially changes the next shift's starting state.

criteria.title: Transfer open hazards, holds, faults, and discrepancies
criteria.fullCredit: Clearly communicates every seeded unresolved hazard, hold, identity discrepancy, equipment fault, or sanitation status that constrains the next shift.
criteria.partialCredit: Transfers the major open conditions but omits one lower-risk context element or needs a permitted prompt to state the current restriction clearly.
criteria.noCredit: Fails to communicate an open condition that could cause unsafe work, prohibited movement, identity loss, or invalid downstream action.

criteria.title: Identify ownership and next actions
criteria.fullCredit: Names the next required action, current owner or notified role, and any condition that must be satisfied before work resumes or closes.
criteria.partialCredit: Names the next action but needs a permitted prompt to identify ownership or the condition for resuming/closing the work.
criteria.noCredit: Hands off an unresolved condition with no clear next action or assigns decision authority to a role that does not have it in the supplied scenario.

criteria.title: Use closed-loop, fact-based communication
criteria.fullCredit: Uses the supplied read-back/cross-check method and separates confirmed facts from hypotheses so sender and receiver share the same controlled starting state.
criteria.partialCredit: Handoff is understandable but needs one permitted prompt to confirm read-back, source cross-check, or fact-versus-hypothesis wording.
criteria.noCredit: Relies on one-way ambiguous communication, presents an unconfirmed hypothesis as fact, or leaves the receiver with conflicting starting information.

criticalErrors: Deliberately falsifies, fabricates, or forces a cultivation, identity, inventory, or traceability record.
Bypasses an explicit hold, quarantine, restricted-entry, or other supplied access-control instruction.
Attempts protected equipment servicing, energized technical work, or repair outside the stated Technician I authority.
Knowingly continues an explicit unsafe condition after the supplied procedure requires stopping or escalation.
Causes avoidable unrecoverable plant or material identity loss by ignoring a detected identity discrepancy.

scoringAnchorPolicy.partialCreditRule: Partial credit means one-half of the criterion's available points. The domain score is the sum of criterion points; these anchors improve scoring consistency but do not create a separate domain pass/fail standard.

learnerWorkflow.overview: Apply Course 1 as one connected cultivation workflow while conditions change during a simulated shift. Learners must preserve safety, identity, traceability, authorization boundaries, record integrity, and handoff quality as new information appears.
learnerWorkflow.academicUse: The practical framework is public academic course content. It may be studied without authentication and used for simulation, supervised-lab, or workplace-equivalent learning and evaluation. Personal assessor results remain private learner records.
preparationSteps: Complete the Course 1 lessons, workbook activities, and low-stakes practice before attempting an evaluated practical.
Review the six Course 1 Field References and know which one applies to hazards, biosecurity, controlled work, traceability, equipment, and records/handoff.
Practice producing all seven required evidence outputs using the Course 1 workbook templates without inventing missing facts.
Be ready to explain when work must stop, what can proceed within Technician I authority, and what must be escalated to another role.
Expect conditions to change during the simulated shift and reassess earlier decisions when new status, identity, sanitation, equipment, or record information appears.

stages.title: 1. Pre-task review
stages.summary: Recognize hazards, access restrictions, work-order limits, identity risks, PPE needs, and operator authority before work begins.

stages.title: 2. Status and sanitation change
stages.summary: Reassess work when one restriction changes but another remains active, and verify exact sanitation-product authorization before substitution.

stages.title: 3. Recurring equipment fault
stages.summary: Stay inside the operator-care boundary, record the fault timeline, and escalate repeated unresolved conditions without unsupported diagnosis.

stages.title: 4. Record integrity
stages.summary: Correct records while preserving original history and distinguish observation time from later entry time without backdating.

stages.title: 5. Closed-loop handoff
stages.summary: Transfer unresolved holds, identity discrepancies, equipment status, sanitation status, and next actions using two-way read-back and source cross-checking.

supportResources: Course 1 remediation matrix and instructor coaching when assigned
learnerWorkflow.boundary: This is Course 1 practical learning and performance evidence. It is separate from the Technician I credential examination and does not by itself issue a professional credential.
